meaning:
εἴσ-οδος, -ου, ὁ
(ὁδός) [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא ;]
1. a means of entering, place of entrance: Heb.10:19, 2Pe.1:11 (cf. Westc., He., l.with; MM, Exp., xii; but see infr.).
2. a going in, entrance: Act.13:24; with genitive loc., Heb.10:19 (Thayer, see word; but see supr.); before εἰς, 2Pe.1:11 (Mayor, in l.; Thayer; but see supr.); πρός, 2Th.1:9 2:1.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: before his coming, when John had first preached the baptism of repentance to Israel.
For they themselves report concerning us what kind of a reception we had from you, and how you turned to God from idols, to serve a living and true God,
Having therefore, brothers, boldness to enter into the holy place by the blood of Jesus,
For thus you will be richly supplied with the entrance into the eternal Kingdom of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.
